description: Large synthetic scRNA-seq UMAP embedding — designed to produce a long CPU-bound tool call (30-90s) with GPU fully idle
prompt:
Perform a UMAP embedding on a large synthetic single-cell dataset using Python. Do everything in one code block. Steps:
1. Generate a count matrix: 30000 cells x 3000 genes. Use numpy.random.seed(42). Draw counts from numpy.random.negative_binomial(n=5, p=0.5, size=(30000, 3000)). Add a random per-gene base mean: multiply each gene column by numpy.random.lognormal(mean=1.0, sigma=1.5, size=3000).
2. Normalize each cell to 10000 total counts (divide each row by its sum, multiply by 10000) then apply numpy.log1p.
3. Select the top 500 genes by variance across cells.
4. Run PCA to 30 components using sklearn.decomposition.PCA(n_components=30, random_state=42) on the 30000x500 matrix.
5. Run UMAP: import umap; reducer = umap.UMAP(n_components=2, n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, random_state=42); embedding = reducer.fit_transform(pca_result). This will take 30-90 seconds — that is expected.
6. Run KMeans with 8 clusters (sklearn.cluster.KMeans(n_clusters=8, random_state=42, n_init=10)) on the 2D UMAP embedding.
7. Print the cluster sizes as a sorted table (cluster_id, n_cells).
Do not generate any plots. Report only the cluster sizes table.
notes: Designed to maximize GPU bubble visibility. UMAP on 30k cells x 30 PCs uses pure CPU (umap-learn), takes 30-90s, GPU goes fully idle during that window. All required packages (numpy, sklearn, umap-learn) are pre-installed in biomni-sglang as scanpy dependencies. The prompt is a single explicit recipe — agent should need only 1-3 execute calls. KMeans on 2D is fast (<1s). Expect GPU bubble fraction 10-30% depending on how many LLM turns the agent uses.
